Research study for cancer survivors

What is the study about?

The purpose of this study is to develop a digital health tool that helps cancer survivors find recipes and meal ideas that support healthy living, which can then be a resource for cancer survivors.

Study led by Dr. Jean Reading at the University of Illinois Chicago, Department of Family and Community Medicine.

Study Title: Evaluating the Usability of a Technology-based Cancer Prevention Support Tool (ThriveWell) for Cancer Survivors

What is involved?

If you agree to participate and are eligible, you will be asked to complete surveys on your demographics, health, and technology use, and join a 60-75 minute focus group (via Zoom or in-person depending on scheduling and preferences).

During the session, you will:

  • Try out ThriveWell, a digital health tool, by completing simple tasks
  • Share your thoughts about the tool by completing surveys

Who can participate?

In order to participate in this study, you must meet all of these criteria:

  • You are 18 years of age or older
  • You were diagnosed with non-metastatic cancer within the last 10 years
  • You are able to access the internet and are reachable by telephone
  • You possess a device to use for study-related activities
  • You are able to read and write in English
  • You have completed primary cancer treatment (surgery, chemotherapy, radiation) at least 3 months ago
